Seeded 2026-08-09 from experiments/roadmap.md (prior-evidence column), findings.md, diagnosis.md Q01/Q02 and Vahidi 2025 (arXiv:2506.13799). Ranked by expected value / cost. The ideator extends this file; it must dedup against autoresearch/killed.json first.

items.title: HARDWARE RE-BASELINE вЂ” re-measure the champions on this machine before any cycle
items.hypothesis: Not a hypothesis вЂ” a prerequisite. Every number in sota.json was measured on Apple MPS. Scores and noise floors are hardware-dependent (different kernels, different non-determinism), so on any new device the champions and their sigmas must be re-measured before a single variant is judged.
items.rationale: The whole Phase-7 verdict rule compares a variant to the champion. Comparing a CUDA-measured variant against an MPS-measured champion is exactly the moving-comparator error the auditor exists to catch вЂ” except the auditor cannot see it, because the device is not part of config_hash. The deterministic scorer-parity test (tests/test_metrics.py, 34,751,902) is what carries over between machines; training trajectories do not.
items.method: 1) pytest tests/ -q must be fully green (the scorer parity is the portability anchor). 2) Run the current champions at the screen seeds on all three datasets: H35 on connectome/mouse, H30 on microns/mouse, role=implement. 3) Recompute mean/std per dataset with autoresearch/audit.py. 4) If any champion mean or sigma differs materially from sota.json, update sota.json via update_sota.py --force with the hardware change logged in experiments/log.md, and update the screen_delta_pp values in campaign.yaml to 2x the NEW sigma. 5) Record the device name and torch version in the log entry.
items.kill_condition: Not killable вЂ” it is a gate. If the scorer parity test fails on the new machine, STOP: the environment is wrong and no result from it is admissible.
items.est_cost: cheap-medium (about 9 runs; connectome ~4 min each, microns ~12 min each on MPS вЂ” faster on a discrete GPU)
items.expected_pp: n/a вЂ” this establishes the reference frame, it does not move the metric
items.outcome: Done 2026-08-09 on Windows 10 / RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (CUDA), torch 2.8.0+cu128, Python 3.9.25. Champions re-measured at seeds 42/123/999, role=implement. sota.json and campaign.yaml screen_delta_pp updated; see experiments/log.md.

items.title: The screen seeds are inert for deterministic variants вЂ” is 3x the compute buying anything?
items.hypothesis: For every variant that does not consume RNG, the screen's 3 seeds are three identical runs on this machine, so 2/3 of every screen's wall-clock buys no information. If that holds, the screen can run 1 seed for deterministic variants and keep 3 only for RNG-consuming ones (multi-start, LNS destroy), roughly tripling hypotheses per night.
items.rationale: P01 established it directly: H35 on connectome produced BIT-IDENTICAL best_positions vectors at seeds 42/123/999, and H30 on mouse gave identical scores. The cause is structural, not incidental вЂ” H02/H30/H35 pass init_positions from deterministic greedy-FAS into run_rocket, so make_init_positions (the only RNG consumer) is never called; torch.manual_seed/np.random.seed are set and then nothing draws. The seed-to-seed spread recorded on MPS (connectome sigma 0.0060) was therefore device non-determinism, not seed variance. NOT actioned unilaterally during P01: dropping to 1 seed changes what every future number means and breaks comparability with the whole existing record, so it needs a decision with the evidence in front of it, not a silent protocol edit.
items.method: 1) Programmatically check which variants under src/mfas/experiments/ reach make_init_positions (i.e. do not pass init_positions) вЂ” that is the RNG-consuming set. 2) For 2-3 of the deterministic ones, run 2 seeds on the cheap datasets and assert bit-identical positions. 3) If it holds, propose a protocol amendment: screen at 1 seed for deterministic variants, 3 for RNG-consuming ones, with the classification RECORDED per variant in the log entry so no reader has to guess which regime a number came from. 4) Leave confirm_seeds alone вЂ” confirm is where an RNG variant must show its spread.
items.kill_condition: Any deterministic-classified variant that differs across seeds on any dataset. One counter-example falsifies the classification and the protocol stays at 3 seeds.
prior_evidence: src/mfas/baseline/rocket.py:168 (make_init_positions is skipped when init_positions is given)
items.est_cost: cheap (minutes; mouse + one microns pair)
items.expected_pp: n/a вЂ” this buys throughput, not score, and on this hardware throughput is the binding constraint: microns runs at 3214 s here vs 706 s on MPS, so a 3-seed screen is 3.2 h and a 5-seed confirm 5.3 h. At 1 seed for deterministic variants a full cycle drops from ~8.5 h to ~2.5 h, i.e. from one cycle a day to four.
items.outcome: ADOPTED 2026-08-09 as a protocol amendment (PROTOCOL.md В§ Phase-7.4, campaign.yaml seed_policy). The screen's seed count is now a property of the VARIANT: classifier-deterministic variants run 1 seed on the primaries, everything else 3, mouse always 3 as the tripwire; confirm_seeds unchanged. Made operative by autoresearch/seed_class.py (static call-graph, fail-safe to 'rng') + autoresearch/seed_plan.py + `sweep.sh --auto-seeds`, pinned by tests/test_seed_class.py and tests/test_seed_plan.py. The queue item's own '~8.5 h to ~2.5 h' estimate was WRONG вЂ” it assumed the confirm stage shrank too; the measured screen-only saving is 3.17 h -> 1.06 h. See experiments/log.md P02.
corrections: The item's expected saving assumed confirm shrank as well. It does not, deliberately: re-running a deterministic variant at 5 confirm seeds re-establishes DEVICE repeatability, which is the only variance source left, and keeps every promotion-path CI off a 1-seed pool.

The item's step 3 asked only that the classification be RECORDED per variant. That is necessary but not sufficient вЂ” a policy nobody executes is not a policy, so the classification is now applied mechanically by seed_plan.py/--auto-seeds rather than by an agent remembering to.

items.title: Cycle handoff: the previous cycle was still writing when the driver launched the next one
items.hypothesis: The driver can start cycle N+1 while cycle N is still writing to the worktree, so two cycles briefly share the sandbox. Observed 2026-08-09 during P02: autoresearch/waitfor.sh (21:13:27) and .claude/agents/verifier.md (21:15:37) appeared AFTER the P02 cycle's preflight `git status` (~21:12) and were not its work.
items.rationale: CAMPAIGN.md is explicit that cycles must be disjoint - two writers to sota.json/state.json/queue.json/log.md do not merge mechanically. This overlap was benign (docs and helper scripts only; no GPU run, no results/*.json, stopped at 21:15), but the same race on a cycle-end write would silently lose or interleave a record. Related and possibly the same root cause: the previous cycle died WITHOUT writing experiments/log.md or state.json despite having produced all of P02's artifacts, so P02 had to be reconstructed from files on disk. P01 already fixed the watchdog's inability to kill a native Windows child (kill_tree); this is the complementary question of whether the driver waits for a cycle to finish WRITING, not just for its process to exit.
items.method: 1) Read driver.sh's lock acquisition/release and the cycle-exit path; determine whether .lock/cycle_pid is cleared before or after the cycle's final writes, and whether a cycle that exits non-zero (or is killed) leaves the lock in a state the next cycle accepts. 2) Reproduce with a stub cycle that sleeps past its own lock release. 3) If confirmed, make the handoff strictly sequential (release the lock only after the cycle's commit) and make an unclean exit visible - a cycle that produced artifacts but no log.md entry should leave a marker the next cycle finds, rather than being discovered by mtime archaeology.
items.kill_condition: If driver.sh already serializes correctly and the observed writes are explained by something else (e.g. an unrelated interactive session), record the real explanation and close - the observation stands either way and the explanation belongs in the log.
prior_evidence: experiments/log.md P01 defect 5 (watchdog could not kill a native Windows child)
autoresearch/CAMPAIGN.md В§ Hardware ('One machine at a time')
items.est_cost: cheap (reading driver.sh + a stub-cycle reproduction; no GPU)
items.expected_pp: n/a - protects the record rather than the metric
items.evidence_upgraded: 2026-08-10 (cycle 5): REPRODUCED WITH TIMESTAMPS, no longer mtime archaeology. .claude/commands/research-cycle.md was written at 07:14:01 with cycle-#4-authored content - 6m23s AFTER driver.log recorded 'cycle #4 finished OK' (07:07:38) and 5m23s after it started cycle #5 (07:08:38); cycle #5's own preflight git status at ~07:09 saw a clean tree. Two cycles shared the sandbox for ~5.4 minutes. Benign this time (a docs file), but it proves the driver releases the lock before the cycle's last writes land.
items.outcome: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED 2026-08-15 (commit 91220f6). The lock was never a per-cycle mutex - it is taken once at driver start and released only at driver exit - and `wait $cmd_pid` returning means one process exited, not that the cycle finished writing. That is structural: sweep.sh and detach.sh EXIST to outlive the session, so overlapping writers are by design. What landed: no-op cycle detection (HEAD + history length either side of a cycle), pid-ownership verification in --abort, and a .sweep status file that lets a resuming cycle tell a killed sweep from an unstarted one. What did NOT land: any barrier that makes cycle N+1 wait for cycle N's writes. Best evidence for the remaining race is proto_H42.json (mtime 08:18:50) written 70 min into cycle #5 by cycle #4's detached prototype - not the research-cycle.md timestamp originally cited, which is retrospective text ABOUT cycle #4 written BY cycle #5. Deprioritised because the damage so far is confined to shared scratch, never to results/*.json.

items.title: SCC-decomposed recursive bounded-span insertion (the Vahidi route)
items.outcome: KEEP / CHAMPION on all three datasets, 2026-08-10 (cycle 3). Built as a recursive SCC-topological BLOCK move class (src/mfas/refine/scc_recursive.py) alternated with the champion's single-node sift (src/mfas/experiments/H36.py stage 4). Confirm: connectome 84.0972 (+0.1837 pp vs H35), microns 83.2338 (+0.0276 pp vs H30), mouse 92.9170 (+0.0152 pp). 30 runs, std 0, audit exit 0. Matched-wall-clock control on BOTH primaries shows 36.0x / 13.0x over the champion's own move class, so the gain is the move class and not the added CPU. Gap to the 84.6147 reference: 0.7046 -> 0.5175 pp. NOT converged: the connectome curve is still rising at 31 cycles (+0.214 pp) and ships at 12 -> see H42. See findings.md #6 and experiments/log.md 2026-08-10.
items.hypothesis: Condensing the graph into SCCs, ordering the condensation DAG topologically, and then recursively applying exact-gain insertion WITHIN the giant SCC (rather than over the whole line) recovers a large part of the remaining 0.70 pp to the 84.6147% reference, at bounded cost.
items.rationale: Vahidi 2025 reaches 84.61% on this exact graph with cheap greedy + bounded-span insertion + SCC and NO MIP, so the residual is demonstrably reachable by combinatorial means. Our H22 kill only falsified RANK-window locality (killed.json M4); a structural (SCC) neighbourhood is a different object. dr_tmp/FINDINGS_underrelaxation.md E2 warns that a ONE-SHOT SCC split recovers ~nothing (inter-SCC edges 1.50%, giant SCC 92.82%) вЂ” so the hypothesis is specifically the RECURSIVE within-giant-SCC form.
items.kill_condition: If recursive within-SCC insertion on the giant SCC does not beat the champion sift on the prototype proxy, the decomposition story is dead and we stop paying for SCC machinery.
items.est_cost: medium (SCC via scipy.csgraph is cheap; the recursion is the work)
items.expected_pp: connectome: up to +0.7 (the whole residual) if the Vahidi mechanism transfers; honest estimate +0.1 to +0.4

items.title: Size up the stage-4 alternation budget - the curve was still rising when we cut it
items.hypothesis: H36 ships 12 alternation cycles on connectome because that was the knee of the cost/benefit curve at a moment when the CYCLE's budget was the binding constraint, not the ALGORITHM's. The measured curve was still climbing: +0.192 pp @ 12 cycles / 340 s, +0.214 pp @ 31 / 803 s. The connectome run has ~2700 s of unused headroom under the 3600 s cap, so raising the count is free score with no new mechanism.
items.rationale: This is the cheapest remaining gain in the campaign: no new code, one constant. The honest question it must answer is where the curve actually flattens - the increments were still ~+0.0007 pp/cycle at cycle 30, so there may be meaningfully more than +0.02 pp left. Microns is the opposite case and must be treated separately: it has only ~290 s of headroom (3314 s of 3600 s), so its cycle count cannot rise without either a cheaper inner sift or P05's wall-clock guard.
items.method: 1) Continue the connectome alternation from the stored H36 champion order well past 31 cycles (CPU only, no GPU) until the per-cycle increment is below the 0.012 pp minimum effect size for several consecutive cycles; plot score vs wall-clock. 2) Pick the largest cycle count whose TOTAL run fits comfortably under the warn band, leaving margin for a loaded machine. 3) Re-screen and re-confirm as a normal variant against the H36 champion. 4) Do NOT raise microns until P05 lands.
items.kill_condition: If the connectome curve flattens below the 0.012 pp minimum effect size before the runtime budget binds, the shipped 12 cycles are already at the practical optimum and this closes with a measured saturation curve.
items.est_cost: cheap to size (CPU only, from stored positions); a normal screen+confirm to promote
items.expected_pp: connectome +0.02 to +0.10 beyond H36; microns 0 until P05
items.outcome: KEEP / CHAMPION on all three datasets, 2026-08-10 (cycle 5). Two constants only: the stage-4 inner sift drops to 2 sweeps and the cycle counts are re-sized {connectome 12->77, microns 3->5, mouse 8->32}. Confirm (5/5/20 seeds, all bit-identical): connectome 84.1541 (+0.0569 pp vs H36), microns 83.2409 (+0.0070 pp), mouse 92.9170 (+0.0000). audit exit 0. THE MECHANISM IS ALLOCATION, NOT COMPUTE: at an identical 1200 s budget the cheap inner sift buys +0.0255 pp over the ship split, and at H36's OWN shipped stage-4 wall (317.7 s) it reaches 84.1400 in 309.7 s - better in fewer seconds. Honest split of the shipped connectome gain: +0.0428 pp is free re-allocation, +0.0141 pp is the extra 394 s. COST: microns now crosses the 3400 s warn band on 5/5 runs (3398-3418 s vs H36's 3265-3314), 182 s under the hard cap - see P05, now load-bearing. Gap to reference 0.5175 -> 0.4606 pp. Q1 answered: the connectome curve saturates at ~143 cycles; past 77 the remaining +0.0047 pp is below the 0.012 pp minimum effect size. See findings.md #7 and experiments/log.md.

items.title: The mouse non-inferiority test is mis-specified - it can only be passed by a large improvement
items.hypothesis: The mouse gate cannot do its job as written. audit.py floors sigma at baseline_sigma_pp = 0.2624 pp (the RANDOM-INIT baseline's dispersion on a 148-node graph); with n_comparator = 3 that is SE = 0.2142 pp, so a PROTOCOL CI lower bound above -0.26 requires delta > +0.1599 pp. A NON-INFERIORITY test is therefore passable only by a large IMPROVEMENT, which is backwards: the floor's conservative direction is correct for the primaries (where the risk is a false positive) and inverted for a non-inferiority check (where the risk is an undetected regression).
items.rationale: Observed twice now and waved through both times, which is how a rule quietly stops meaning anything. P02: audit_P02.json mouse protocol_ci_lower = -0.4199, KEEP at delta = 0.0000. H36 (2026-08-10): -0.4047 at delta = +0.0152 pp over 20 seeds with zero dispersion. PROTOCOL.md's decision table does have a 'both primaries confirm, mouse does not' row ('GENERAL WIN with mouse caveat'), so neither cycle was wrong to keep - but a gate whose failure is routine and expected is not a gate, and the next cycle should not have to re-derive that argument from scratch.
items.method: 1) Decide what the mouse gate is actually FOR - detecting a regression on a tiny near-saturated graph - and write the test that detects that: e.g. a one-sided bound on the point estimate against -0.26 pp, or a floor taken from the CHAMPION's dispersion rather than the random-init baseline's, or an equivalence-style test with the floor applied in the non-inferior direction only. 2) Whatever is chosen, verify it against the historical record: it must not retroactively kill H30/H35/H36, and it MUST fire on a genuine mouse regression (construct one and check). 3) Encode it in campaign.yaml + PROTOCOL.md + audit.py's significance block so no future cycle argues it by hand.
items.kill_condition: If no defensible re-specification both clears the historical champions and fires on a synthetic regression, keep the current rule but document in PROTOCOL.md that the mouse PROTOCOL CI is advisory and the decision-table row is the operative rule.
prior_evidence: experiments/log.md 2026-08-10 (H36), section 'The one number that does NOT pass'
items.est_cost: cheap (no GPU; arithmetic plus a synthetic-regression check)
items.expected_pp: n/a - protects the verdict rule
items.narrowed: 2026-08-10 (cycle 5, H42): the diagnosis in this item is WIDER THAN THE DEFECT. The mouse non-inferiority bound PASSED for H42 (protocol_ci_lower = -0.1626 > -0.26) with no change to the test. What changed is the COMPARATOR POOL: protocol_se scales as sqrt(2/n_c), so a 3-seed comparator gives SE = 0.2142 pp (bound -0.42, unpassable) while H36's 20-seed mouse pool gives SE = 0.0830 (bound -0.1626, passable). P02 and H36 both failed it because they were compared against 3-seed mouse pools, not because the statistic is mis-specified. Mouse costs ~5 s/run, so the cheap fix is to REQUIRE a 20-seed comparator pool on mouse before quoting the bound. Re-scope the item to that, and verify it still fires on a synthetic regression.
items.outcome: DONE 2026-08-15. The gate was not merely mis-specified, it was UNPASSABLE: protocol_se = max(comparator_std, 0.2624) * sqrt(2/n_comparator) used the RANDOM-INIT baseline's dispersion as a floor for a pipeline whose real dispersion is 0, and used only the COMPARATOR's n, so the variant's 20 mouse seeds contributed nothing. Clearing -0.26 required delta > +0.16 pp on a dataset PROTOCOL.md itself calls saturated. It returned -0.4047 for H36 - whose mouse score IMPROVED, 92.90180243 -> 92.917014102 - and -0.4199 for P02 at delta exactly 0, and it never once changed a verdict. Re-specified as a real non-inferiority test: se = max(pooled_sd, measurement_resolution_pp) * sqrt(1/n_v + 1/n_c), pooling both arms and flooring at the dataset's own oracle resolution. H36's mouse leg goes -0.4047 -> +0.0152 (PASS); a -0.31 pp regression still fails. Pinned by tests/test_audit_gates.py.

items.title: BLOCKING: stage 4 has no wall-clock guard and microns now runs 3398-3418 s against a 3400 s warn band
items.hypothesis: H36's stage 4 is a fixed CYCLE COUNT, and sweep.sh passes no --time-limit, so when time_limit is None the refinement has no wall-clock guard at all. On microns the run is already 3314 s against a 3600 s hard cap - about 8% margin. A loaded machine, a thermal throttle or a background job does not degrade the run, it OVERRUNS the cap, and the run then fails on usability grounds after burning ~55 minutes of GPU time.
items.rationale: The 3600 s rule exists so that an algorithm that cannot answer within an hour is out of scope. A variant that satisfies it only on an idle machine satisfies it by luck. The fix is cheap and belongs in the refiner, not in each variant: alternate_scc_sift already accepts time_budget_s and honours it - what is missing is a DEFAULT budget derived from the runtime cap when the caller passes nothing. This must not change any confirmed number: a default that never binds on an idle machine leaves H36's 30 confirmed runs bit-identical, and that must be verified, not assumed.
items.method: 1) Give H36 (and any future refinement stage) a default stage-4 wall-clock budget = campaign.yaml runtime.warn_wall_clock_s_per_run minus the elapsed run time, so the refinement degrades gracefully instead of overrunning. 2) Re-run H36 on microns and connectome at seed 42 and assert the score is UNCHANGED on an idle machine (the guard must not bind). 3) Only then make it the default. 4) Consider also having sweep.sh pass an explicit --time-limit so the guard is exercised rather than dormant.
items.kill_condition: If measurement shows the microns wall-clock is stable enough across repeated runs that the margin is not at risk, record the measured spread and close - the observation stands either way.
prior_evidence: experiments/log.md 2026-08-10 (H36), runtime section (microns max wall 3314 s)
items.est_cost: cheap code change; ~1 h of GPU to verify the guard does not bind
items.expected_pp: n/a - protects the runtime invariant
items.progress: 2026-08-11 (cycle 6): THE GUARD IS BUILT, ARMED AND VERIFIED ON 2 OF 3 DATASETS. Root cause was wider than filed: every stage already honoured a wall-clock budget (rocket per epoch, sift per sweep, alternate_scc_sift per cycle) and NOTHING EVER PASSED ONE - sweep.sh calls run_variant with no --time-limit, so time_limit=None made every check a dead branch. eval/runtime_guard.py now resolves a deadline of max_wall_clock_s_per_run - reserve_s (3600 - 150 = 3450 s) whenever the caller gives none; reserve_s is sized from experiments/outputs/proto_P05.json (prologue+epilogue outside the deadline: microns 36.0 s, connectome 20.5 s, mouse 0.1 s) plus the abort granularity, and both margins are pinned by tests/test_runtime_guard.py. It is an ABORT at a stage boundary, never a sizing rule, so the H42 determinism constraint is respected. VERIFIED: guard fires and records exactly what it cut (forced 3 s deadline on mouse -> rocket 2159/5000, sift 2/40, stage4 1/32, degraded=true); guard does NOT fire on connectome (seed 42 bit-identical to the stored confirm vector, 0/136,648 differing, sha b56aa222bedfe958) or mouse (3/3 at 92.917014). audit.py gained a runtime_guard check (FAIL on a truncated run, WARN on pre-P05 records) and still exits 0 on the existing champion evidence.

items.title: BLOCKING: the champion's microns configuration does not fit 3600 s on a loaded machine
items.hypothesis: H42's microns run does not satisfy the campaign's own runtime invariant under ordinary conditions. Its confirmed walls (3397.8-3418.0 s) were measured overnight on a quiet machine. Measured 2026-08-11 under ordinary desktop load, the SAME connectome computation returning a BIT-IDENTICAL result took 1483.9 s against cycle 5's 1226.5-1238.3 s: +20.5%, where cycle 5's own five-run spread was 1.0%. Scaled to microns that is ~4100 s against a 3600 s hard cap. So the microns configuration is inside the budget only when nobody is using the laptop.
items.rationale: The 3600 s rule exists so that an algorithm that cannot answer within an hour is out of scope; a configuration that satisfies it only on an idle machine satisfies it by luck. P05 fixed the DETECTION side of this - the run now aborts at a stage boundary, is flagged `degraded` and is FAILed by audit.py instead of silently overrunning - but a guard cannot make an over-budget configuration fit. Left alone, the consequence is concrete and blocking: every future microns run on a working machine returns truncated and audit-FAILing, so no variant can be promoted on microns at all, whatever its score. Note this is NOT an argument for weakening the cap or the guard - it is an argument that microns' compute allocation was sized against an unrepresentative measurement.
items.method: 1) Re-measure the champion's microns wall on an idle machine AND under representative load, >=2 runs each, to replace the single 20% data point with a spread (cheap in wall-clock terms, expensive in hours - schedule it). 2) Attribute the cost with the per-stage timings that now land in results/*.json (variant_attrs, P06a): microns is 80,000 Rocket epochs against connectome's 20,000, so stage 1 is the obvious suspect and stage 4 is only ~88 s of ~3400. 3) The cheapest honest lever is queue item S01 - if the gradient phase is largely ceremonial, cutting microns' epochs restores the margin at no score cost, and S01 is explicitly allowed to run during Phase 1 as SIZING. 4) Any change to the shipped microns configuration is a normal variant and goes through the full ladder; do NOT hand-edit constants into the champion.
items.kill_condition: If a repeat measurement on an idle machine shows the 20% figure was an artefact of one contended window - i.e. microns' wall stays within a few percent of 3400 s across repeated runs under realistic load - then the margin is thinner than comfortable but real, and this closes with the measured spread recorded. The observation stands either way.
prior_evidence: experiments/log.md 2026-08-11 (P05), section 'THE FINDING THIS CYCLE DID NOT EXPECT'
items.est_cost: cheap to measure (2-4 microns runs, ~1 h each); the fix is S01-shaped and is a normal variant

items.title: Cycle-triggered under-relaxation (fix the microns regression, make H35 a general win)
items.hypothesis: Switching from Jacobi (alpha=1) to under-relaxed (alpha<1) sweeps ONLY once a period-2 limit cycle is actually detected вЂ” instead of unconditionally after k_full=6 sweeps вЂ” recovers H35's connectome gain without the -0.0019 pp microns loss, making it a clean 3-dataset GENERAL WIN.

Detection (candidate score alternating between two values / mover set oscillating) is cheap and removes the hand-tuned constant.

items.title: Gauss-Seidel / block-sequential exact-gain sift
items.hypothesis: Replacing the simultaneous (Jacobi) rebuild with sequential (Gauss-Seidel) or block-sequential updates вЂ” each node re-inserted against the CURRENT order, not the stale one вЂ” converges where Jacobi limit-cycles and reaches a strictly better fixed point than under-relaxation.
items.rationale: Under-relaxation (H35) is the textbook cure for a Jacobi 2-cycle; Gauss-Seidel is the other one, and usually the stronger. The open question is cost: the current kernel is vectorized-NumPy over all nodes at once, so a naive GS loses the vectorization. Block-sequential (K blocks, Jacobi within a block, sequential across blocks) is the practical middle and is a tunable interpolation between the two.
items.kill_condition: If block-sequential at any block count fails to beat H35 on the connectome prototype, or if the per-sweep cost exceeds the runtime budget.
items.est_cost: medium (needs a blocked kernel to keep vectorization)
items.expected_pp: connectome +0.05 to +0.3 (speculative)
items.outcome: PROTOTYPE GATE 2026-08-16 -> KILLED (experiments/outputs/proto_H38_connectome.json, proto_H38_mouse.json). Block-sequential loses to the champion's under-relaxed Jacobi at EVERY block count and under BOTH damping schedules, from the same greedy-FAS start on connectome: K=2 damped -0.04685 / undamped -0.55312; K=4 -0.07366 / -0.11775; K=8 -0.13827 / -0.10571 pp. Same sign on mouse. It also costs K times more per sweep. PARITY: the K=1 arm reproduces sift_underrelaxed EXACTLY (83.44721 connectome, 93.08288 mouse), so every K>1 difference is the mechanism and not the harness. THE CONFOUND WAS TESTED, NOT ASSUMED AWAY: the first grid damped the block-sequential arms with alpha=0.7, which is the cure for the JACOBI collision that Gauss-Seidel does not have by construction - handicapping the arm with a treatment for a disease it lacks. Re-running undamped does NOT rescue it; at K=2 it is 12x worse. So damping helps sequential schemes too, which means under-relaxation's benefit is broader than the 'Jacobi 2-cycle cure' that underrelax.py's docstring attributes it to.
items.revival_if: HONEST LIMITATION of this gate: at K<=8 each sub-step still moves ~n/K nodes simultaneously (68,324 at K=2), so the Jacobi collision is still present and the PURE Gauss-Seidel limit K=n was never reached. The trend across K=1,2,4,8 is monotonically AWAY from the champion, which is evidence against the limit rather than for it, but it is not a proof. A revival would need a kernel that reaches small blocks affordably - restricting jacobi_best_gaps to a block's incident edges (a block of n/K nodes touches ~m/K edges) recovers an O(m) sweep and would make K in the thousands testable. Only worth building if some other evidence suggests the limit behaves differently from the trend.

items.hypothesis: Moving contiguous SEGMENTS (or coherent groups) of nodes as a unit reaches orders that no sequence of single-node insertions can, because the Rocket<->best difference is a distributed long-range reordering rather than a set of independent misplacements.
items.rationale: The gap structure (diagnosis Step 2) is a distributed reordering with Kendall-tau 0.61 and rank-distance p50 ~22,580 вЂ” consistent with whole regions being in the wrong place. Single-node exact-gain insertion is, by construction, blind to a move that is only profitable jointly.

items.title: Re-allocate the microns budget: cut Rocket epochs 80,000 -> 20,000 and spend the freed 2,338 s on stage-4 cycles
items.hypothesis: On microns the last 60,000 Rocket epochs are 71.7% of the run's wall clock and buy only +0.01919 pp, while stage 4 runs at 5 cycles against the ~143 that connectome's stage-4 curve needs to saturate. Moving that budget across the GPU/CPU boundary - 20,000 epochs plus ~140 alternation cycles at the same total wall clock - reaches a strictly better score than the champion's 83.24085, because every score move this campaign has produced came from stage-4 refinement and none from the gradient phase.
items.rationale: Measured tonight, not assumed (experiments/outputs/proto_P07.json, log.md 2026-08-16). The microns epoch curve is convex in log-epochs up to 20,000 (per-doubling increments +0.00942 -> +0.01464 -> +0.02234 -> +0.06375 pp) and then knees hard: the two doublings 20,000 -> 80,000 buy +0.01919 pp between them, at 121.8 s per 0.001 pp. Cutting to 20,000 frees 2,337.7 s of a 3,258.2 s run; at the measured microns stage-4 rate of 17.2 s/cycle (86.00 s / 5 cycles) that is ~136 extra cycles. This is the SAME mechanism that made H42 champion - allocation, not compute - applied across a different boundary: H42 re-allocated WITHIN stage 4, H43 re-allocates FROM the gradient phase INTO it. It also closes P07 by sizing rather than by a guard: the run drops to ~920 s + refinement, so the 3,450 s deadline stops binding on the one dataset where it binds. CORROBORATED 2026-08-16 by a per-stage marginal-value table built from logged runs with zero new compute (experiments/log.md, 'marginal value of a second'): microns stage 4 returns 4.33e-4 pp/s at its margin while the microns Rocket tail returns 0.08e-4 pp/s. H43 moves seconds from the worst row of that table to the best, at a ratio of 54:1. The same table pre-empts the neighbouring 'stage 3 is truncated, raise the cap' idea - the stage-3 tails return 1.73e-4 (connectome) and 0.82e-4 (microns) pp/s, i.e. strictly less than stage 4 - so that variant is deliberately NOT queued. QUALIFIED 2026-08-16 by the connectome grid: from 20,000 to 40,000 epochs pure Rocket improves +0.13560 pp and stage 3 improves +0.03314 pp while the FINAL score falls -0.00666 pp. The refinement stack is not monotone in the quality of its input, so the seconds this item moves from Rocket into stage 4 cannot be assumed to convert at the marginal rate. The kill condition's requirement to MEASURE the stage-4 recovery curve rather than extrapolate it is therefore load-bearing.

items.title: Exact-gain JOINT PAIR relocation - the move our sift is provably blind to (Vahidi Alg 2, vectorised)
items.hypothesis: The champion's sift relocates nodes INDEPENDENTLY: jacobi_best_gaps takes each node's own argmax over its exact insertion profile. It is therefore blind by construction to a move where neither endpoint of a heavy backward edge profits alone but both profit from meeting. Take a backward edge (u,v) with rank[v] < rank[u], extract BOTH endpoints, and re-insert them adjacent as u,v at the best split r inside the interval between them. EXACT gain (corrected 2026-08-16 - see scout_L01_addendum; the earlier 'total_u(c)+total_v(c)+w_uv' form stated here was a heuristic, not exact): Delta(r) = (w_uv - w_vu) + sum_{j<=r}[w(n_j->v) - w(v->n_j)] + sum_{j>r}[w(u->n_j) - w(n_j->u)], where n_1..n_t are the nodes strictly between v and u. Verified by independent derivation: the interval is a contiguous position range, so by the contiguous-block lemma segment.py already proves, no edge with an endpoint outside it can flip; the n_j keep their relative order so nothing among them flips; only edges incident to u or v flip, each on exactly one side of r. Delta(r) is PIECEWISE CONSTANT in r and changes only at neighbours of u or v, so the optimal split costs O(d(u)+d(v)) INDEPENDENT of interval length - mean total degree on connectome is 83. The claim: sweeping this over the heaviest backward edges, batched over disjoint intervals, reaches a strictly better fixed point than the champion's stage 3 + stage 4.
items.rationale: This is the load-bearing move of the method that produced the reference solution's family (autoresearch/lit/vahidi-2025.md, retrieved from the arXiv HTML AND the authors' notebooks). Their Alg 2 pops the heaviest backward edge (u,v), takes the ENTIRE rank interval between v and u - uncapped - and tries every cut r, re-inserting u and v adjacent at one common cut, with an exact closed-form gain by prefix/suffix sums. We already have every ingredient: jacobi_best_gaps (src/mfas/refine/insertion.py:91) builds the exact piecewise-constant profile per node, and select_disjoint_moves (src/mfas/refine/segment.py:315) is the disjoint acceptance rule. The gap structure supports it: diagnosis.md puts median rank-distance at ~22,580, and the paper's own table gives mean back-edge length 20,536 - this move is global-range, which is exactly what M4's directive asks for. It also satisfies H31's stated revival condition verbatim: a STRUCTURE-AWARE destroy operator (guided by heavy backward edges, not random) with an exact-gain rebuild.
items.kill_condition: PROTOTYPE GATE, cheap and decisive, run BEFORE building anything: over the top-K heaviest backward edges in the champion's connectome order, measure the fraction whose JOINT argmax differs from both independent argmaxes. If that fraction is <1%, the move class is not distinct from the existing sift and the item dies for free. Second gate: if it is distinct but the realised gain per second is below the stage-4 marginal rate of 3.45e-4 pp/s, it loses on allocation even if it works.

items.scout_L01_addendum: MERGED 2026-08-16. Scout L01 arrived at this same mechanism independently from arXiv:2506.13799v1 Algorithm 2 and from the ABSTRACT of the 2026 follow-up (Vahidi & Koutis, 'Interval-Based Refinement Algorithms for Large-Scale Weighted Feedback Arc Set', SSRN 6221201, posted 2026-02-11 - full text 403, NOT read). Two independent derivations landing on the same move is the strongest novelty signal the queue has had. Three things this item did not yet contain. (A) A CORRECTNESS WARNING ABOUT THE STATED OBJECTIVE. The hypothesis above proposes maximising total_u(c) + total_v(c) + w_uv over a common cut c using jacobi_best_gaps' per-node profiles. That is a HEURISTIC, not the exact gain: total_u(c) was computed with v still at its current position and total_v(c) with u still at its, so the u-v interaction is double-counted and each profile uses a stale position for the other endpoint. The EXACT gain of extracting both and re-inserting them adjacent at split r inside the interval is Delta(r) = (w_uv - w_vu) + sum_{j<=r}[w(n_j->v) - w(v->n_j)] + sum_{j>r}[w(u->n_j) - w(n_j->u)], where n_1..n_t are the nodes strictly between v and u. Proof: the interval is a contiguous position range, so by the contiguous-block lemma no edge with an endpoint outside it can flip; the n_j keep their relative order so no edge among them flips; only edges incident to u or v flip, each on exactly one side of r. This matches the paper's stated Delta = w_uv - w_vu + in_v - out_v - in_u + out_u with in/out taken over the two sides of the split. USE THE EXACT FORM - the campaign's whole accounting discipline (predicted gain == realised oracle delta, as tests/test_refine_segment.py asserts) depends on it. (B) THE COST ARGUMENT IS BETTER THAN 'medium'. Delta(r) is PIECEWISE CONSTANT in r and changes only at block positions that are neighbours of u or v, so the optimal r costs O((d(u)+d(v)) log(d(u)+d(v))) INDEPENDENT OF INTERVAL LENGTH. Mean total degree on connectome is 2*5,657,719/136,648 = 83. This is emphatically NOT an O(n^2) method. (C) THE BATCHING RULE THE 2026 ABSTRACT NAMES. 'A dynamic program to select large sets of non-overlapping backward-edge intervals, then refining them in parallel' = weighted interval scheduling (sort by right endpoint, binary-search the last compatible interval, O(k log k)). Disjoint contiguous intervals compose ADDITIVELY by the same lemma, so the realised delta equals the sum of the selected gains and the whole set applies in one vectorised sweep - the optimal version of what select_disjoint_moves does greedily today. Full notes and citations: autoresearch/lit/notes-vahidi-flywire.md sections 3.2 and 4; autoresearch/lit/hypotheses.md rank 1. Honest scope estimate added by L01: connectome +0.05 to +0.30 pp, midpoint +0.15, on the grounds that this is the published mechanism behind the 0.7524 -> 0.8461 jump.
items.outcome: PROTOTYPE GATE 2026-08-16 -> KILLED AS FILED (experiments/outputs/proto_H45_pair_connectome.json). All 1,178,821 backward edges scanned on the champion's order. DISTINCTNESS: YES - 3,498 pairs have a strictly positive exact gain and 989 of them (28.3%) are invisible to the champion's sift because neither endpoint profits alone; the best single move spans 92,958 positions (68% of the line). EXACTNESS: 25/25 against the frozen oracle after a real bug was caught and fixed (aggregating per-edge events instead of per-POSITION manufactures unachievable splits and inflates gains - first run scored 1/18). REACHABLE GAIN: greedy packing +0.00100 pp, OPTIMAL interval-scheduling DP +0.00193 pp (1.93x better - H41's greedy select_disjoint_moves leaves ~half its gain unpacked, a free fix if that machinery is revived). +0.00193 pp is 6.2x below the 0.012 pp minimum effect size. WHY IT DIED: it was filed as a BOLT-ON to a converged order. The champion is already a joint fixed point of insertion + SCC, so only 0.30% of backward edges admit any improving pair move. In the reference family the SAME move is the PRIMARY refiner from a 75.24% greedy start and is credited with the climb to 84.61%. We measured it in the one regime where it has nothing left to do.

items.title: Coarse multilevel k-block permutation - generalise the segment swap to k blocks at coarse scales
items.hypothesis: H41's segment move is a 2-block adjacent swap capped at L,d <= 1024 (1.5% of the connectome line). Generalising it to a k-block permutation at COARSE levels - blocks of thousands of nodes - covers the scale at which the diagnosis says the disagreement actually lives, and is still EXACT by the same contiguous-block lemma segment.py already proves.
items.rationale: The contiguous-block lemma in src/mfas/refine/segment.py generalises from 2 blocks to k: partition the line into k contiguous blocks, and one np.bincount over all edges gives the full k x k inter-block weight matrix, so the exact gain of ANY permutation of those blocks is read off that matrix with no rescoring. At small k the optimal permutation is exhaustive (k <= 8 is 40,320). Cost is O(m) per level - seconds at connectome scale - which makes the prototype almost free. Vahidi's Alg 4 is the same idea at a fine scale (their published run uses x=6, l=6, i.e. groups of ~2.9 nodes and a window of ~18 positions); the untested regime is the coarse one, blocks of 3,800-22,775 nodes, which is where diagnosis.md's ~22,580 median rank-distance sits.
items.kill_condition: One O(m) pass: build the k x k matrix at each coarse level from the champion's connectome order and compute the best permutation's exact gain. If the best gain across all levels is below the 0.012 pp minimum effect size, the whole coarse-block family is closed - and it is closed by a measurement that costs seconds, not a screen.
prior_evidence: src/mfas/refine/segment.py (the contiguous-block lemma and the bincount/prefix-sum machinery, already proven exact against the frozen scorer)
autoresearch/lit/vahidi-2025.md (their Alg 4 - same idea, fine scale only)

items.scout_L01_addendum: MERGED 2026-08-16, second independent derivation of the same mechanism. Four additions. (A) NAME THE COARSE PROBLEM CORRECTLY AND THE LITERATURE OPENS UP. Permuting K contiguous rigid blocks is EXACTLY the Linear Ordering Problem on the K x K inter-block weight matrix W, and the transformation is EXACT rather than a relaxation - a property this objective admits and that minimum-linear-arrangement does not (see autoresearch/lit/notes-scalable-fas-and-negatives.md section 2 for why edge-contraction coarsening does NOT transfer and position-block coarsening does). That matters because the entire LOP metaheuristic literature is built for dense instances of exactly this size: the 2026 state-of-the-art benchmark (Fagiolo, Baioletti, Santucci, 'Linear Ordering Problem: Time for a Change', arXiv:2605.31051, PPSN 2026) tops out at n = 300 with a Theta(n^2) neighbourhood-evaluation acceleration - useless at n = 136,648 and exactly right at n = K. (B) DO NOT USE EXHAUSTIVE PERMUTATION. 'k <= 8 is 40,320' caps the move class at 8 blocks. Held-Karp subset DP, f[S] = max_{j in S} f[S\{j}] + sum_{i in S\{j}} W[i][j], gives the EXACT optimum in O(2^k k^2): k = 16 costs ~1e6 operations against 16! = 2e13. Vahidi's Algorithm 4 brute-forces x! and is therefore capped near x = 5-6, which is precisely the regime this item calls untested - the DP lifts the cap by a factor of 2-3 in k for free. (C) A CHEAPER INNER SOLVER FOR LARGE K. For K in the thousands the DP is out and the LOP insertion neighbourhood on D = W - W^T is the right tool: moving block a from coarse position p to q gains -sum_{b in (p,q]} D[a][b] rightward or +sum_{b in [q,p)} D[a][b] leftward, which is a prefix sum along the current coarse order - O(K) for ALL target positions at once, O(K^2) per full sweep, ~0.1 s vectorised at K = 4096. Build W sparsely (scipy.sparse.coo_matrix on block(src)*K + block(tgt), at most m = 5.66M nonzeros) and densify only for K <= 4096 (16.8M float64 = 134 MB). (D) CYCLE THE BLOCK BOUNDARIES. A node sitting on a boundary is invisible to both sides, exactly as an edge cut by a split is in scc_recursive. Cycle a deterministic OFFSET across rounds, in the same no-RNG register as DEFAULT_SPLIT_FRACS, so a boundary node at one round is interior at the next. WORTH RUNNING FIRST OF ALL THE QUEUED MOVE-CLASS ITEMS: it is the cheapest decisive test in the queue and either outcome is a diagnosis the campaign does not have - it partitions the remaining 0.4606 pp into coarse mis-ordering of whole regions vs fine mis-ordering inside regions, which tells H45 and H47 where to look. Record the number in diagnosis.md whichever way the gate goes. Full notes: autoresearch/lit/notes-vahidi-flywire.md section 3.4, autoresearch/lit/notes-lop-and-ocm.md, autoresearch/lit/hypotheses.md rank 2. L01's honest range: connectome 0 to +0.15 pp, midpoint +0.05.

The champion's order has no coarse-scale misordering whatsoever - the remaining 0.4606 pp is not a block-permutation problem at any scale from 17,081 to 68,324 nodes, which is exactly the band diagnosis.md's rank-distance percentiles (p25 8,290 / p50 22,580 / p75 54,432) pointed at. items.title: Exact subset-DP ordering at the SCC recursion's leaves (the champion currently optimises nothing below 32 nodes)
items.axis: discrete refinement / exactness of an existing move class
items.hypothesis: SccRecursiveRefiner._refine returns immediately for any block of size <= min_block = 32 and always preserves each SCC's internal relative order, so the champion's block refiner never optimises anything small. Solving those leaves EXACTLY by Held-Karp subset DP recovers weight that both the single-node sift and the block refiner leave behind.
items.rationale: Vahidi 2025 Algorithms 3 and 5 both exhaustively permute any sub-SCC with |S| <= 9 to maximise internal forward weight; we do nothing at all below 32. Replace exhaustive permutation with subset DP - f[S] = max_{j in S} f[S\{j}] + sum_{i in S\{j}} w(i->j) - giving the EXACT optimum internal order of a k-node block in O(2^k k^2) instead of O(k! k): k = 16 costs ~1e6 operations against 16! = 2e13, so the exact threshold can be raised from 9 to 16 at a fraction of the cost. NOVELTY vs killed.json: this is NOT a rank window - it is the TERMINAL CASE OF THE SCC RECURSION, i.e. structurally decomposed, which is M4's own named revival condition. It also adds no new class; it makes an already-confirmed class exact where it currently does nothing. H22 was single-node re-insertion in a window; this is the exact optimum over all k! orderings of a structurally-derived block, and a single-node sift can be at a fixed point while the block is far from its optimum. M1-M3, M5-M7 untouched. HONEST SELF-CHECK, recorded before the test: M4 is the strongest prior AGAINST this one - it measured net recoverable weight within a window as <= 0 for W >= 100, and although k <= 16 is far below that, the champion's sift is already single-node optimal, which removes most of what a tiny window can hold. I expect this to die at its gate. It is queued because the gate costs almost nothing and the number it produces - how much of the residual is intra-window at all - is a diagnosis worth owning.
items.method: 1) PROTOTYPE GATE, CPU ONLY, NO GPU: from the stored H42 champion connectome positions, for k in {8, 12, 16}, tile the line with disjoint contiguous windows of size k, DP-optimise each, sum the exact gains and verify the total against the frozen oracle. Disjoint contiguous windows compose additively, so the sum IS the realised delta. 2) If it clears, implement src/mfas/refine/leaf_exact.py as a SUBCLASS of SccRecursiveRefiner overriding only the base case - scc_recursive.py must stay untouched so the champion remains bit-reproducible - plus src/mfas/experiments/H47.py. 3) COMMIT THE MODULE BEFORE THE SCREEN.
items.kill_condition: If the total exact gain is below 0.012 pp at every k in {8, 12, 16}, the leaves are already locally optimal and this is dead with 0 GPU spent.

items.title: The reference ROUTE run standalone: ratio-greedy init + iterated exact-gain pair relocation
items.hypothesis: Run the reference family's route on its own terms rather than bolted onto the champion: ratio-greedy init, then iterated exact-gain pair relocation with optimal interval-scheduling batching, no Rocket, no sift, no SCC. Measured against our own Rocket-free arm (83.87975), not against the champion.
items.rationale: Divergent-mode item after 5 consecutive kills. H45's gate showed the move class is real and distinct - 989 improving moves invisible to our sift, the best spanning 68% of the line - but that it has nothing left to do on our CONVERGED order. In the reference family it is the primary refiner from a cheap start and is credited with 75.24 -> 84.61.

items.outcome: MEASURED 2026-08-16 -> KILLED AS IMPLEMENTED, with a precise diagnosis that is worth more than the verdict (experiments/outputs/proto_H50_connectome.json). connectome: init 74.61730 -> 75.29304 after 40 sweeps (2,150 s), i.e. +0.67573 pp, leaving it 8.59 pp BELOW our own Rocket-free arm and 8.86 pp below the champion. Every sweep exact (predicted == realised, oracle-checked). mouse climbed 88.38256 -> 92.84280 (+4.46 pp in 30 sweeps) and had NOT converged, so the move class itself is strong. THE BOTTLENECK IS THROUGHPUT UNDER DISJOINTNESS, NOT THE MOVE CLASS. Across the 40 sweeps 4,018,567 positive-gain candidates were found and 4,193 applied - 0.104%. The ratio degrades from 0.730% at sweep 0 to 0.032% at sweep 39, because a pair move's interval spans the distance between a backward edge's endpoints (mean 20,536 positions per the reference's own table) and disjoint intervals of that size barely fit on a 136,648-position line. Reaching even 83.87975 at the observed rate needs ~1,086 more sweeps, about 16 hours. ARCHITECTURAL FINDING: this campaign's refiners are all 'compute every gain vectorised, apply a maximal DISJOINT batch'. That is correct and fast for single-node moves, whose intervals are tiny, and it is structurally unable to exploit interval moves. The reference's Alg 2 applies moves ONE AT A TIME from a heap with incremental updates - a sequential architecture our batched one cannot emulate.
items.revival_if: Only via H51: sequential application with an order-maintenance structure. The move class and its exact gain are verified; what is missing is the ability to apply ~100,000 moves per pass instead of 60.

items.title: Sequential pair relocation with an order-maintenance structure (unblock H50's throughput)
items.hypothesis: The exact-gain pair relocation move is verified and abundant - ~100,000 positive-gain candidates exist on the connectome order at every sweep - but the campaign's batched-disjoint application can only realise 0.1% of them. Applying them SEQUENTIALLY, each against the updated order, realises the rest and is what the reference family actually does.
items.rationale: H50 measured the blocker exactly: 4,018,567 candidates found, 4,193 applied (0.104%), because pair-move intervals average tens of thousands of positions and disjoint intervals of that size barely fit on the line. Sequential application is blocked for us by one thing: naively applying a pair move rewrites the rank of every node in the interval, which is O(interval) and averages ~20,536 positions. An ORDER-MAINTENANCE structure (Dietz-Sleator labelling) gives O(1) amortised insert/delete and O(1) order comparison, so moving two nodes costs O(1) and the gain kernel's 'is this neighbour inside the interval' test stays O(1) per neighbour. That converts the per-move cost from O(interval) to O(d(u)+d(v)), which is the same bound the gain computation already has.
items.kill_condition: Two gates. (1) Cheap: on the connectome order, apply the top-N pair moves SEQUENTIALLY with a naive O(interval) rank rebuild for N=1,000 and measure the realised gain. If sequential application of 1,000 moves does not beat the ~60 that a disjoint batch fits by a wide margin, the throughput story is wrong and H51 dies before the data structure is built. (2) If it passes, build the order-maintenance version and require the whole pipeline to beat 83.87975 - our own Rocket-free arm - before it is compared to the champion at all.
items.est_cost: high - a real data structure, but gate (1) is an afternoon
items.expected_pp: unknown; the external claim for this route is +0.46 pp over our champion, provenance unverified
items.outcome: CONFIRMED and PARTLY PROMOTED 2026-08-17 as variant H52. items.title: Ratio greedy init ((out_w+1)/(in_w+1)) instead of greedy-FAS - a +6.3 pp better start at the same cost
items.hypothesis: Vahidi's Algorithm 1 - peel nodes by score(u) = (out_w+1)/(in_w+1) with a max-heap, updating scores on removal - reaches 75.24% on this exact connectome graph. Our H02 greedy-FAS warm start reaches 68.9134% (measured tonight: proto_S01_connectome.json arms[epochs=0].pure_pct). That is +6.33 pp of starting quality at the same asymptotic cost. The claim is that with a REDUCED or ABSENT gradient phase, the better start survives into the refined score.
items.rationale: M6-init-is-flat says the init->plateau curve is flat on connectome and better-init-alone has a <=0.06 pp ceiling. That was measured THROUGH Rocket - the plateau washes the init out, which is exactly what M6 describes. Tonight's epoch grid measures the Rocket-free and Rocket-reduced regime directly for the first time (connectome epochs=0 reaches 83.87975 from a 68.9134 start), so the init question is re-opened on evidence rather than by assertion. M7-expensive-warmstarts-lose does NOT cover this: it forbids EXPENSIVE global linear-algebra embeddings (trophic, magnetic Laplacian, 304-507 s); a ratio greedy is the same O(m log n) heap peel as the greedy we already run. Note the campaign's own Phase-6 conclusion, 'greedy+sift is the design; no smarter init earns its cost', was drawn without ever testing a second cheap greedy. PROMOTED to priority 0 on 2026-08-16 by the H45 gate. That gate established the pair-relocation move class is real and distinct but has almost nothing left to do on a converged order, which reframes the whole reference route as INIT-then-refiner. The two measured endpoints now sit side by side: our refiner from greedy-FAS 68.91343 reaches 83.87975, theirs from ratio-greedy 75.24 reaches 84.61. H48 isolates whether that difference is the init or the refiner, at the cost of one CPU pass, and it is the cheapest question in the queue with a bearing on the mission target.
items.kill_condition: Two gates, both cheap. (1) Reproduce the init score alone: if the ratio greedy does not beat 68.9134% on connectome by a wide margin, the premise is dead at the cost of one CPU pass. (2) If it does, run it through the epochs=0 arm of the sizing harness. If the refined score does not beat 83.87975%, then M6 extends to the Rocket-free regime too - a genuinely useful negative - and the item dies.

items.outcome: SCREEN FAILED 2026-08-16 -> KILLED (variant H49, module committed at d589883 BEFORE the runs). connectome 84.140276 vs champion 84.154095 = -0.01382 pp (threshold +0.012); microns 83.243515 vs 83.240853 = +0.00266 pp (threshold 0.002, passes); mouse 92.790860 vs 93.082880 = -0.29202 pp, WORSE than the -0.26 non-inferiority margin. Fails both the connectome gate and the mouse gate. THE SCIENCE: the init was +5.70387 pp better (74.61730 vs 68.91343), still +0.03456 pp ahead after stage 3, and -0.01382 pp BEHIND after the full pipeline. The advantage was not merely washed out, it INVERTED - the third instance in 24 h of the refinement stack being non-monotone in the quality of its input. M6-init-is-flat is confirmed and EXTENDED - it holds through the full pipeline, not just through Rocket's plateau, and the ceiling is not merely low but can be negative.

items.title: Run records discard per-stage timings (sweep.sh confirm_seeds part is fixed)
items.hypothesis: Two independent gaps, both found while auditing H42, both of which force a cycle to INFER numbers it should be able to READ. (a) eval/run_variant.py does not persist history.attrs into results/*.json, so per-stage scores and timings - which every multi-stage variant since H30 computes at runtime - are discarded. H42's central runtime claim ('the +107 s on microns is entirely stage 4') therefore rests on an inference from stages 1-3 being byte-identical, not on a measurement, and no auditor can check it. (b) sweep.sh --role confirm does not read campaign.yaml confirm_seeds; it silently defaults to '42 123 999', so a confirm launched the obvious way runs 3 seeds instead of 5/5/20 and looks complete.
items.rationale: (a) is a provenance hole in the one direction the campaign is currently spending its budget - stage-4 refinement - and it defeats audit.py's whole purpose of re-deriving claims mechanically. (b) is a live foot-gun: cycle 5 hit it, noticed only because it had just read the config, and had to top up the missing seeds in two extra sweeps. A cycle that did not notice would have promoted a champion on a 3-seed confirm while believing it ran the configured 5/5/20, and audit.py would have reported n=3 without anything flagging that as wrong.
items.method: 1) Persist history.attrs (or an explicit stages[] block: name, score, pct, wall_s) into results/*.json. It is additive - do NOT touch the frozen scorer or harness contract - and verify a re-scored run is unchanged. 2) Have audit.py report per-stage wall-clock when present, so runtime attribution becomes a check rather than a narrative. 3) Make sweep.sh --role confirm read confirm_seeds from campaign.yaml per dataset (it already does per-dataset seeds for --auto-seeds, so the plan format supports it), and make an explicit --seeds with role=confirm either an error or a loud warning. 4) Consider having audit.py FAIL when a confirm pool is smaller than the configured confirm_seeds.

items.title: The campaign's two significance criteria disagree for the first time - decide which governs
items.hypothesis: Not a hypothesis - an operator decision. campaign.yaml carries TWO thresholds for a connectome promotion and on 2026-08-17 they disagreed for the first time: H52 scored +0.02093 pp, which CLEARS min_promotion_delta_pp (0.012) and FAILS the PROTOCOL CI (threshold 1.96 * 0.0189 * sqrt(2/5) = 0.02343 pp). H36 (+0.1837) and H42 (+0.0569) both cleared the higher bar, so the conflict never surfaced before.
items.rationale: The PROTOCOL CI floors sigma at baseline_sigma_pp = 0.0189, a frozen-baseline noise floor inherited from the MPS era when the pipeline was measured as stochastic. On CUDA these pipelines never draw from `seed`: H52's connectome pool is 5 runs with ONE distinct value and std exactly 0, re-scored exactly by the frozen oracle. So the test asks whether a deterministic delta exceeds a historical STOCHASTIC noise floor from a different device era. That may still be the right conservatism - a deterministic pipeline can be deterministically wrong, and 0.0189 pp is a reasonable estimate of how much a re-measurement might move - but it is a judgement, and it is now BINDING on real results rather than hypothetical ones. NOTE THE TEMPTATION AND WHY IT WAS REFUSED: the threshold scales as sqrt(2/n), so running 7 connectome seeds instead of 5 would have lowered it to 0.0198 pp and passed H52 unchanged. On a pipeline with std = 0 those extra seeds carry ZERO information; shrinking an artificial SE to admit one's own result is exactly what these gates exist to prevent. It was not done, and this entry exists so the decision is the operator's rather than the agent's.
items.kill_condition: Operator picks one of: (a) keep both gates as-is and accept that gains in the 0.012-0.023 pp band are unpromotable on connectome; (b) re-derive baseline_sigma_pp on THIS device for a deterministic pipeline, which would likely collapse it toward measurement_resolution_pp and make min_promotion_delta_pp the binding rule; (c) keep the CI but state a fixed seed count in the protocol so n cannot be chosen after seeing the delta. Do NOT resolve by re-running with more seeds.

It FAILS CLOSED; before it, a pool with zero dispersion needed no robustness evidence at all. It can only refuse.

THE EVIDENCE THE OPERATOR NOW HAS (4.2 h GPU, 5 paired points, experiments/outputs/proto_P09_connectome.json; 25 mouse points in proto_P09_mouse.json): relabelling is an exact isomorphism (verified - the parity anchor re-scores to 34,751,902 under every permutation used); the champion's own connectome score moves over 84.11418066-84.15550043, sigma 0.019124 pp, and one labelling beats the canonical figure quoted since 2026-08-10; that sigma is within 1.2% of the fossil baseline_sigma_pp = 0.0189, so the constant's MAGNITUDE was right and its APPLICATION was not - it applies a MARGINAL dispersion UNPAIRED to two arms that share the nuisance almost exactly, then divides by sqrt(n) over five identical reruns. The PAIRED delta sigma is 0.002011 pp, 9.5x tighter; the paired one-sided 95% lower bound on the mean delta is +0.015626 pp against a 0.012 bar. Taken in its OWN unpaired frame the old rule is incoherent rather than conservative: effective n = 1 (P02), so the self-consistent threshold would be 0.053 pp, more than double what was applied.
THE DECISION IS UNCHANGED IN SHAPE: (a) keep both gates and accept that 0.012-0.023 pp is unpromotable on connectome; (b) retire the PROTOCOL CI for degenerate pools, leaving the relabelling gate plus min_promotion_delta_pp; (c) keep the CI but fix n in the protocol. Note (c) cures the n-manipulability at zero cost and still refuses H52. NO NEW RUNS ARE NEEDED for any branch - ratification alone flips H52's connectome leg to promotable.

items.title: Relabelling multi-start: harvest the dispersion that seeds do not have
items.hypothesis: Running the champion pipeline on R randomly relabelled copies of the graph and keeping the best-scoring order by the oracle beats a single canonical-labelling run, because relabelling is the only source of score dispersion this deterministic pipeline has.
items.rationale: MEASURED THIS CYCLE, not argued (experiments/outputs/proto_P09_connectome.json). Node relabelling is an exact symmetry - isomorphic graph, identical achievable scores - yet the champion H42's connectome score moves over 84.11418066 to 84.15550043 across 5 labellings, sigma = 0.019124 pp, range 0.041 pp. One relabelling (r=3, 84.15550043) already produces a STRICTLY BETTER H42 order than the canonical labelling does (84.15409511), i.e. +0.00140 pp for no algorithmic change whatsoever. Expected best-of-R gain over the mean for a normal is 0.56 sigma at R=2 and 0.85 sigma at R=3: ~+0.011 and ~+0.016 pp. For scale, the whole of H52's stage 5 is +0.0175 pp mean.
items.novelty: H01 is KILLED on this exact axis ('restarts / multi-start: no score dispersion across seeds to harvest, see M3') and its kill is CORRECT and untouched: seeds are inert here (P02 - make_init_positions is unreachable, seeds 42/123/999 are bit-identical). The revival condition H01's kill implies is 'find a source of dispersion that actually exists', and this cycle measured one. This is a different randomisation, not a retry of the same one.
items.method: 1) PROTOTYPE, cheap: mouse and an SCC subgraph, R in {2,3,5}, confirm the best-of-R curve tracks the order statistics of the measured sigma. 2) The runtime is the whole difficulty and must be stated first: H42 connectome is ~1150 s against a 3450 s guard deadline, so R=2 fits comfortably, R=3 is at the wall, and microns (~3400 s) has room for NOTHING - so this is a connectome-and-mouse variant at best, and a microns REGRESSION risk via truncation. 3) Compute-matching: CAMPAIGN.md's 'a gain that is really extra compute' applies in full - the control is the same wall-clock spent on more stage-4/stage-5 cycles at a single labelling, which H42's own sizing curve says saturates. 4) Selecting the best of R by the oracle score is the SAME use the baseline already makes of it (CAMPAIGN.md rule 4, 'track the best-scoring positions seen'), not leakage.
items.kill_condition: If best-of-R at matched total wall-clock does not beat a single run given the same seconds, on both primaries, this is extra compute rather than a mechanism and it dies.

items.title: Confirm spends ~1.7 h re-running an identical computation; buy relabellings with it instead
items.hypothesis: For a variant the classifier calls deterministic, 4 of the 5 connectome confirm seeds carry no information about the algorithm, and the same GPU hours spent on relabellings would carry a great deal.
items.rationale: P02 established that these pipelines never draw from `seed` and that this device reproduces a seed bit-identically, so the 5-seed confirm re-establishes DEVICE repeatability and nothing else - campaign.yaml says so explicitly and keeps them for that reason. As of P09 a primary promotion on a degenerate pool ALSO needs a >=4-relabelling study (~4.2 h on connectome). Those two evidence budgets overlap: 5 identical runs cost ~1.7 h of connectome and answer one narrow question that 2 runs answer as well. Trading 3 of them for relabellings is close to cost-neutral and strictly more informative, because the relabelling arm subsumes the repeatability check (an identity row that reproduces the record IS the repeatability evidence). ALSO now carrying the P09 debt the critic surfaced: the SITTING champions predate the relabelling gate and have no studies, so re-auditing H36/H42 under --gate promotion FAILS on relabel.<ds>. That is a real gap in the record, not a bug. Cost to close: ~4.2 h per connectome pair and ~9.4 h per microns pair.

items.title: Pre-registrations must be committed before launch, not left untracked
items.hypothesis: A pre-registration whose precedence rests on an mtime is not a pre-registration.
items.rationale: Cycle 9's critic checked and found `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- 'experiments/outputs/proto_P09*'` returns NOTHING: the P09 pre-registration existed only as an untracked working-tree file when the study ran. Its ordering was verifiable in fact (mtime 16:04:31 vs launch 16:04:34, and the first data row could not exist before ~17:04), and the critic confirmed it - but both the mtime and the state.json line recording it are writable by the agent that benefits from them. The Track-2 S2 entry of 2026-08-25 did this correctly: 'sealed and committed in ef6900e BEFORE the run'. CLAUDE.md invariant 5 already requires a commit per experiment; this makes the ordering auditable instead of asserted.
